newsitem.title: GERMANY: Euro to be weak if tax not harmonised - German SPD.
newsitem.headline: Euro to be weak if tax not harmonised - German SPD.

text.p: German opposition leader Oskar Lafontaine warned on Monday the basis of Europe's planned single currency would be undermined if tax systems across the continent were not harmonised.

"If a harmonisation of tax systems does not take place, then European economic and monetary union will be based on weak foundations," he told a meeting of his Social Democrats (SPD) on European policy.

Lafontaine said it was unacceptable for European Union countries to compete against one another for jobs and investment by cutting taxes and social contributions for employers, leaving workers to pick up the tab.
"All Social Democratic governments must oppose this development and correct it."
Lafontaine said the SPD supported the introduction of the single currency according to the timetable and criteria laid down in the Maastricht Treaty.
The new currency, the euro, would help put an end to the currency market fluctuations which had damaged all European economies in the past, he said.
"We want the currency union because we expect long-term benefits for the labour market all over Europe."
